meta.name: teaching_video_criteria
meta.based_on: v1.0 (24-metric A-F) + 2026-06-27 fixes: F2 reframed deduction-only, C4 decoupled from correctness, D2 credits animation craft, F3 pace-not-duration.
meta.purpose: One deduplicated, learning-science-grounded criteria tree that BOTH evaluators score against: rubric_coverage_check.py (single-call) and AI_student/phase_2/batch_audit_processor.py (multi-agent). Replaces batch_audit's 30 overlapping flags; each construct is measured exactly once, at one node.

scale.1: Absent: completely missing or severely fails this aspect.
scale.2: Emerging: basic attempt but inconsistent, limited effect.
scale.3: Adequate: meets baseline expectations, no obvious issues.
scale.4: Proficient: done well, clear design intent, consistent.
scale.5: Exemplary: outstanding, could serve as a model for this aspect.

meta.scoring_notes: Canonical per-metric score is the 1-5 above. batch_audit's multi-agent split is preserved via the per-metric `evaluator` field (objective=Agent2 content/logic judge, subjective=Agent3 persona sim). batch_audit's objective hard-error findings (the old critical_fact_error / language gate) act as evidence and as score FLOORS on A1 (any uncorrected critical error caps A1<=2; non-English caps A1=1), not as a separate parallel scale.

tm_dimensions.accuracy: Teaching Monster: Accuracy — is what is taught correct and complete?
tm_dimensions.pedagogical_logic: Teaching Monster: Pedagogical Logic — is it structured, scaffolded, and explained soundly?
tm_dimensions.adaptation: Teaching Monster: Adaptation — is it tuned to THIS learner's level, prior knowledge, and pace?
tm_dimensions.engagement: Teaching Monster: Engagement — multimedia design, delivery, and active-learning that sustain attention.

meta.channels: Each metric lists `needs` (modalities the judgment requires: transcript / audio / visual) and `evaluator` (which batch_audit agent owns it).

A1_factual_accuracy.definition: Are spoken facts, formulas, data, AND on-screen figures/diagrams/equations factually correct for what the video teaches?

anchors.1: Pervasive wrong/misleading content; a learner would draw false conclusions.
anchors.3: No substantive errors; any nitpicks negligible.
anchors.5: Exemplary correctness; visuals and statements are precise and well-matched to the science/math.

A1_factual_accuracy.floors: Any uncorrected critical error (confidence>=0.8) caps A1<=2. primary_language in {mixed, non_english} caps A1=1.

A2_topic_coverage.definition: Does the video cover all topics implied by its title/learning goal, at appropriate depth (not absent, not so thin as to be essentially absent)?

anchors.1: Multiple core topics absent; fails its stated scope.
anchors.3: All implied topics present with adequate coverage.
anchors.5: Notably richer than the title implies; goes meaningfully beyond stated scope.

A3_logical_structure.definition: Are concepts presented in a logical, coherent sequence, with each idea ordered after its prerequisites and conclusions following from their support?

anchors.1: Concepts arrive before their prerequisites; conclusions unsupported; order obstructs understanding.
anchors.3: Sound order; no idea needs a later one to make sense.
anchors.5: Deliberately built sequence; each step motivates the next.

A4_learning_objectives.definition: Does the video state, near the start, what the learner will be able to do or understand afterwards (explicit objectives / 'what you'll learn')?

anchors.1: No statement of purpose anywhere; learner cannot tell what success looks like (or stated objectives misrepresent the content).
anchors.3: Objectives or a clear 'what you'll learn' framing stated (or the single-concept goal is self-evident for a short clip).
anchors.5: Crisp objectives that are explicitly returned to and fulfilled.

A5_curriculum_completeness.definition: Relative to the Key Learning Points in the course requirement, does the video cover every required point (not just title-implied topics)? Judge against the title if no requirement is given.

anchors.1: Most key learning points missing or only named without explanation.
anchors.3: Most key points covered; one or two missing or only superficial.
anchors.5: All key points covered with appropriate depth, and connections between them made explicit.

A6_bloom_alignment.definition: Does the cognitive depth actually delivered match the target Bloom's level in the course requirement? Penalize BOTH under-shooting (only definitions when 'apply' is required) AND wasteful over-shooting (heavy derivation when only 'understand' is required).

anchors.1: Severe mismatch: delivered depth far below or wastefully above target throughout.
anchors.3: Roughly on target; several sections at the wrong cognitive level.
anchors.5: Precisely calibrated to the target level, depth deliberately tuned to it.

B1_signaling.definition: Does the video use visual cues — highlights, arrows, boxing, color-coding, zoom, pointer/cursor, progressive reveal — to guide attention to the relevant part of the screen while narrating?

anchors.1: Narration systematically references specific visual elements with no cueing; viewer cannot follow without pausing.
anchors.3: Basic signaling present and sufficient, or content simple enough that explicit cueing is unnecessary.
anchors.5: Consistently timed, precise signaling; viewer always knows where to look.

B2_segmenting.definition: Is the video segmented at cognitive turning points — with recaps, signposted transitions, or natural pauses between chunks — so the learner can assimilate before the next idea, without information overload?

anchors.1: One undifferentiated stream, no chunk boundaries or recaps; cognitively overwhelming.
anchors.3: Reasonable chunking; topic shifts signposted or paced so the learner keeps up.
anchors.5: Deliberate segmentation with crisp recaps at every turning point.

B3_coherence.definition: Is the video free of irrelevant or distracting material — decorative animations with no teaching payload, tangents, excessive branding, seductive details (Mayer's coherence principle)?

anchors.1: Eye-candy/tangents replace substance; learner asks 'why am I watching this?'.
anchors.3: Largely on-task; at most one minor decorative distraction.
anchors.5: Every element earns its place; nothing extraneous.

B4_modality_integration.definition: Do narration and visuals COMPLEMENT each other (not redundant word-for-word text) and stay SYNCHRONIZED — the right picture present when the words need it, never fighting or ignoring each other?

anchors.1: Visuals repeatedly contradict, lag, or distract from narration; learner must ignore the screen.
anchors.3: Narration and visuals generally aligned; at most one harmless mismatch.
anchors.5: Tight, complementary integration; words and visuals each carry distinct, synchronized load.

C1_examples_analogies.definition: Does the video use analogies, concrete examples, or multiple representations to make abstract concepts intuitive?

anchors.1: Pure abstraction; no examples, analogies, or alternate representations.
anchors.3: At least one effective example/analogy for the key concept.
anchors.5: Rich, well-chosen examples and analogies throughout that genuinely build intuition.

C2_scaffolding_strategy.definition: Does the video build from what the learner knows to what they need (known->unknown bridge), motivate each formula/step (intuition, derivation sketch, limiting case), and avoid unjustified logic leaps?

anchors.1: Formulas presented as facts with zero scaffolding; derivations riddled with unexplained leaps.
anchors.3: Definitions and reasoning present; at most one key 'why' skipped.
anchors.5: Every step motivated and bridged from prior knowledge; standout exposition.

C3_conceptual_procedural_balance.definition: Is there an appropriate balance between 'understanding why' (concept) and 'knowing how to do' (procedure), rather than a drill of worked calculations with thin theory?

anchors.1: Almost pure calculation/procedure (>85%); a worked-examples playlist with no conceptual spine.
anchors.3: Theory and procedure both present and reasonably balanced for the goal.
anchors.5: Concept-first spine; calculations subordinate, illustrating rather than dominating.

C4_visual_explanation_power.definition: Do the visuals do real explanatory work — actively reveal a mechanism (how/why), not merely decorate or restate the conclusion as text? Static/decorative where a dynamic build is needed scores low; a visual the concept would be harder to grasp WITHOUT scores high. (Judges explanatory USE of visuals only — geometric/factual correctness of the figure is scored under A1, not here.)

anchors.1: Visuals static or decorative; all conceptual work done by narration; OR narration actively ignores/devalues the visual.
anchors.3: Key concepts have supporting visuals that illustrate the idea.
anchors.5: Visuals carry genuine explanatory load; the chosen visual approach makes the concept clearer than words alone could.

C4_visual_explanation_power.pilot_validated: Confirmed 2026-06-02: drops cleanly when narration stops leveraging / devalues the visual (C4txt_severe -> -0.67 swing). The OLD visual-only degradation (curve removed) did NOT move it — detection requires the defect to surface in narration.

D1_speaker_delivery.definition: Is the speaker's delivery conducive to sustained attention — expressive (not flat/monotone/robotic) AND FLUENT (not halting, stuttering, or full of false starts/repetitions)?

anchors.1: Persistently soporific (drone/monotone) OR so disfluent — stutters, restarts, repeated words, broken cadence — that following the delivery is a strain.
anchors.3: Clear and followable; neither notably flat nor notably disfluent.
anchors.5: Energizing, well-paced, fluent delivery that actively sustains attention.

adds: disfluency / halting delivery (NEW — closes the D4txt pilot gap; the old intelligibility+continuity flags could not catch stuttering because clear-but-stuttered speech is still intelligible and gap-free)

D2_visual_design.definition: Is the overall visual design clean, readable, uncluttered, well-composed (hierarchy/alignment/spacing), free of generic 'AI-slop' imagery, with legible on-screen text/labels — and is any animation/motion smooth and well-crafted? (Whether the visual HELPS understanding is C4, not here.)

anchors.1: Cluttered, poorly composed, illegible text, or dominant generic AI art throughout.
anchors.3: Clean and readable; at most one weak slide.
anchors.5: Polished, consistent, professional composition — and smooth, well-crafted animation where present — that aids reading.

D3_narrative_and_learner_agency.definition: Does the video establish WHY the topic matters, build a question -> exploration -> resolution arc, and position the learner as an active discoverer rather than a passive recipient?

anchors.1: No motivational framing; content starts abruptly; learner purely passive.
anchors.3: Clear relevance ('why this matters') plus a summary/takeaway.
anchors.5: Sustained narrative arc and 'aha' moments; learner consistently framed as discoverer.

D4_audio_production.definition: Is the audio signal clear and continuous — decodable words (no mumbling/clipping/masking noise) and smooth joins (no abrupt voice-identity shifts, overlaps, gaps, or robotic cut-offs at transitions)?

anchors.1: Largely unintelligible or pervasive splice/dropout artifacts dominate listening.
anchors.3: Clear and continuous; at most one minor artifact.
anchors.5: Studio-clean, seamless audio throughout.

D4_audio_production.optional_signal: May be backed by a deterministic DSP measurement (clipping count, SNR, dropout seconds) since signal-level artifacts are sub-perceptual to the LLM (see D4 pilot).

E1_embedded_questions.definition: Does the video include genuine questions, quizzes, or pause-and-think prompts during viewing (not rhetorical questions the narrator immediately answers)?

anchors.1: Fully passive; no embedded questions or pauses.
anchors.3: At least one genuine posed question with room to think.
anchors.5: Well-placed checks for understanding at the right cognitive moments.

E2_generative_prompts.definition: Does the video prompt learners to DO something generative — predict, explain, draw, summarize, 'try it yourself'?

anchors.1: No invitation to generate anything; watch-only.
anchors.3: At least one real generative prompt with room to act.
anchors.5: Recurrent generative activity woven through the lesson.

E3_worked_examples.definition: Does the video provide worked examples with progressive fading toward independent practice (full worked -> partially worked -> learner does it)?

anchors.1: No worked examples where the procedure clearly needs them.
anchors.3: Worked examples present and clearly stepped.
anchors.5: Deliberate fading from fully-worked to independent practice.

F1_vocabulary_appropriateness.definition: Are technical terms introduced at a level appropriate for this learner's grade/background, with definitions when needed (undefined jargon beyond their stated knowledge counts against)?

anchors.1: Pervasive undefined jargon beyond the persona's level.
anchors.3: Terms generally pitched right; key new terms defined.
anchors.5: Vocabulary precisely tuned to the persona; every new term scaffolded.

F2_prerequisite_awareness.definition: Does the video stay WITHIN this persona's prior knowledge? Scored by DEDUCTION: penalize ONLY when the content assumes or requires knowledge the persona LACKS (esp. items under the persona's 'Lacks'). Do NOT require the video to actively mention, review, or re-teach prerequisites — a video pitched correctly at the persona scores high even if it never revisits background. This measures over-assumption, not the presence of prerequisite coverage.

anchors.1: Core steps require knowledge the persona lacks; the persona would be lost and give up.
anchors.3: Mostly within the persona's reach; a few spots assume something under 'Lacks' but can be patched while watching.
anchors.5: Stays entirely within the persona's prior knowledge; nothing is assumed beyond their background (no active prerequisite review required to earn this).

F3_pacing_fit.definition: Is the information density and speaking rate appropriate for this persona's grade and Focus Time — not too rushed, not padded, not over-rehashing what they already know? Judge by on-screen PACE / information density relative to Focus Time, NOT by raw total duration: a longer video that stays within the persona's pace and finishes the material is fine.

anchors.1: Unwatchable for this persona: Focus Time blown by padding, or so dense/fast that constant rewinding is needed.
anchors.3: Occasionally too fast/slow but finishes within Focus Time without major frustration.
anchors.5: Rhythm and density ideally matched to this persona's attention and baseline.

crosswalk_old_batch_audit_flags._comment: Every one of the 30 batch_audit flags maps to exactly one canonical metric (the home where that construct is now measured ONCE). Flags previously double/triple-counted are listed at their single new home.
crosswalk_old_batch_audit_flags.scaffolding_failure_level: C2 (was double-counted in accuracy+logic; now once)
crosswalk_old_batch_audit_flags.missing_scaffolding_level: C2 (was a 3rd copy in adaptability; merged)
